title: 7 Best Video Interview Software Compared in 2027
summary: Compare the best video interview software for volume hiring: recorded, live, and AI-led tools, with pricing, G2 ratings, and limits.

## What is video interview software?


Video interview software is a hiring platform that runs the first or second interview round over video and stores each answer for review. It adds set questions, scoring, candidate links, and ATS sync that a meeting app lacks. For volume teams, it replaces most first-round phone screens.


**What it usually includes:**


- Fewer first-round calls for recruiters and hiring managers
- The same questions for every candidate
- Candidates answering at any hour


Some teams call it a digital interviewing software. It is one stage inside the wider[candidate screening software](https://www.peoplebox.ai/blog/candidate-screening-software/) category.


## What types of video interview software are there?


There are three types of video interview software: recorded, live, and AI-led. Recorded tools send set questions that a recruiter watches later. Live tools host a scheduled call. AI-led tools, by video or phone, hold the conversation, ask follow-ups, and return a scorecard.


Type How it works Recruiter workload Best for Watch out for


Recorded (one-way) Candidate records answers to set questions on their own time A recruiter watches every answer Early screening for simple roles Reviews pile up at volume; no follow-up questions


Live Scheduled video call inside the tool, recorded with consent Full interview length plus scheduling Final and panel rounds Scheduling across shifts and time zones


AI-led (video or phone) An AI interviewer asks questions, follows up, and scores, also called an AI video interview or automated video interview Reading the scorecard Interviewing every applicant at volume Needs clear scoring criteria and a human final decision


For a deeper look at the recorded format, also called asynchronous or pre-recorded interviewing, see[one-way video interviewing software](https://www.peoplebox.ai/blog/one-way-video-interview-software/) . An[AI interviewer](https://www.peoplebox.ai/ai-interview-software/) runs the AI-led format, and[AI interview tools that run the whole interview](https://www.peoplebox.ai/blog/ai-interview-tools/) compares the tools in that group. “Video screening” means using any of the three at the first round.

#### A rule of thumb for choosing a video interview software:


1. Pick recorded when every candidate answers the same questions.
2. Pick live when a hiring manager needs a real conversation.
3. Pick AI-led when recruiters spend their hours on first-round calls.


## What features should you look for in video interview software?


A video interview platform should send a mobile link that needs no app or login, ask the same questions in the same order, score answers against criteria you set, write results back to your ATS, and export recordings and transcripts. For hourly roles, add text or phone options for candidates without a good camera.


1. **Phone-friendly interviews:** Candidates should be able to join from a phone with just a link, without logging in or downloading an app.
2. **Multilingual interviews:** Candidates should be able to answer in their own language, and the tool should transcribe the answers in that language. Ask each vendor which languages it supports.
3. **Role-based question sets:** Every candidate for a role gets the same questions in the same order, as in a[structured interview](https://www.peoplebox.ai/blog/structured-interview/) , so recruiters can compare answers side by side.
4. **Scoring with transcript and evidence:** Answers are scored against criteria you set, and the transcript shows the evidence behind each score, so a recruiter can check it.
5. **Two-way sync with your ATS and HRIS:** The tool pulls applicants from your ATS and HRIS and sends scores, transcripts, and stage changes back, so nobody copies results by hand. See how video interview software connects to your ATS.
6. **Interview export and privacy:** You should be able to export interviews in bulk, set how long recordings are kept, and control who can view or share them.
7. **Interview scheduling:** Only live rounds need scheduling, where a recruiter and candidate meet at a set time.
8. **Identity checks:** Add identity verification only if the role needs it.

### When is a meeting app enough instead of video interview software?


- If you only run final or panel rounds live.
- If you run fewer than 10 interviews a month.
- If your ATS already handles scheduling and scorecards.
- If you do not need recorded screening, scoring, or sync.


A meeting app falls short if you need set questions, candidate links that need no scheduling, scoring, or ATS write-back for every applicant. In that case, video interview software is the better fit.


## How do candidates experience recorded, live, and AI-led interviews?


Candidates finish video interviews when the link opens on a phone, the interview is short, and they can pick a time or a channel. Hourly applicants often apply to several jobs at once, so a long recorded interview with no follow-up loses them. Test completion in your pilot before you sign.


- Keep first-round interviews under 15 minutes.
- Let candidates choose a time, including nights and weekends.
- Offer phone or text for applicants without a camera.
- Tell candidates how answers are scored and who reviews them.

## How should you choose video interview software?


Choose video interview software by starting with your slowest hiring step, then matching the interview type to it. Check that the tool connects to your ATS, works on a phone, scores against your own criteria, and lets you export your data. Then run a 30-day pilot at 2 or 3 locations.


Problem What to look for Question to ask a vendor

District and location leaders spend hours on first-round calls Automation: interviews that run and score without a leader Does it interview every applicant with no leader involved, and how fast is the score ready?


Leaders screen differently at each location Structure: one locked question set per role Can I lock one question set per role, in the same order for every candidate?


Candidates get lost between the job board and the ATS Sync: applicants in, results back to the ATS Does it connect to my ATS or HRIS, take applicants in, and save scores and transcripts to their record?

Before you sign, confirm:


- ATS or HRIS on the vendor’s list

Video interview software should connect to your ATS in both directions: it pulls applicants and job details in, then writes scores, transcripts, video links, and stage changes back. Check which ATS or HRIS the vendor supports, which fields sync, and how fast. A tool that does not write back becomes a second system your recruiters update by hand.

## How do video interview tools handle fraud, bias, and compliance?


Video interview tools reduce fraud and bias risk when they confirm identity, flag copied or scripted answers, ask every candidate the same questions, and keep a human in the final decision. AI scoring in hiring is regulated in some US places, such as New York City, so check the rules with counsel before launch.


- An identity check at the start of the interview.
- Follow-up questions that expose scripted answers.
- The same questions and scoring criteria for every candidate in a role.
- Human review before any rejection.
- Bias audit results, candidate notices, and consent for recordings, available on request.
- Retention limits and access permissions for recordings.
- Accommodations for candidates with disabilities: offer a non-video option, extra time, and a way to request changes before the interview.


This is information, not legal advice.


## How do you switch video interview software without losing candidates?


To switch video interview software without losing candidates, export every recording, transcript, and score first, then confirm the new video interview tool writes to the same ATS fields. Run both tools in parallel for 2 to 4 weeks, move one job family at a time, and keep the old system read-only until audits close.


1. Export data and check retention rules.
2. Map ATS fields and stages.
3. Rebuild question sets and criteria.
4. Pilot at 2 or 3 locations.
5. Move job families one at a time.
6. Switch off invites in the old tool.


The recruiting operations lead owns the move. Plan for 4 to 8 weeks.


## How much does video interview software cost?


Video interview software pricing depends on interview volume, recruiter seats, the interview types you turn on, and add-ons such as AI scoring or assessments. Budget for the platform fee, setup, ATS integration, and recruiter time to build questions. Compare the video interview solutions above on these factors, then choose the one that fits best.


## Which video interview software is right for your team?


The best video interviewing software for your team depends on what your hiring needs most. Recorded tools suit low volume and simple roles. Live tools suit final rounds. AI-led tools suit teams that must interview every applicant, across shifts and locations, without recruiters.


Start with your slowest step and fix that first. Test your top 2 tools at 2 or 3 locations for 30 days, and compare completion and recruiter hours. If you want an AI interviewer for that pilot,[see how Peoplebox.ai runs it](https://www.peoplebox.ai/ai-recruiter/) .


## FAQs


### What is video interview software and how does it benefit hiring?


Video interview software runs interviews over video and stores the answers for review. It cuts first-round calls, asks every candidate the same questions, and lets candidates answer at any hour from a phone.


### What is the best video interview software?


The best video interview software depends on your volume and roles. Spark Hire, Willo, and Hireflix suit recorded screening, HireVue and VidCruiter suit large teams, and Peoplebox.ai and Jobma suit AI-led interviews.


### Is there free video interview software?


Some online interview software offers a free plan or a free trial, usually capped by jobs or interviews each month. Free plans rarely include AI scoring or ATS sync, so check limits before you commit.


### What platforms are used for virtual interviews, and is Zoom or Teams enough?


Teams use meeting apps such as Zoom, Google Meet, and Microsoft Teams, or dedicated virtual interview software. Meeting apps work for live rounds but have no set questions, scoring, candidate links, or ATS sync.


### What is video screening software?


Video screening software is video interview software used at the first round to filter applicants. Candidates answer short screening questions on video, and the tool or a recruiter scores answers before anyone books a call.


### What is the difference between one-way and live video interviews?


A[one-way video interview](https://www.peoplebox.ai/blog/one-way-video-interview-software/) sends set questions that candidates record on their own time. A live video interview is a scheduled call with a person. One-way suits early screening, and live suits final rounds.


### How does AI score a video interview, and how do recruiters review it?


AI scoring turns each answer into a transcript and rates it against set criteria. Recruiters open the stored recording through a shared link showing the score and evidence, and can override any score.


### Are AI-scored video interviews legal in the US?


AI-scored interviews are legal in the US, but some places add rules. New York City requires bias audits and notices for automated hiring tools. Ask each vendor for audit results, and check requirements with counsel.


### How long does it take to set up video interview software?


Setup usually takes days to a few weeks. A recruiting operations lead usually owns it: connect your ATS, write questions and criteria per role, then run a 30-day pilot using the Pilot Scorecard.


### Can candidates take a video interview on a phone?


Yes, if the tool sends a mobile link. Look for interviews that open from a text or email in a phone browser with no app or login, plus a phone-call option for hourly candidates.


### Can video interview software detect cheating or AI-assisted answers?


Some can reduce it. Look for identity checks, proctoring, and follow-up questions that expose scripted or AI-assisted answers. No tool catches everything, so keep a person reviewing results before any candidate is rejected.


### What’s the best video interview software for remote or multi-location hiring?


For remote or multi-location hiring, choose remote interview software with one locked question set per role, interviews that score without a local leader, and ATS write-back. Compare tools by team size in the fit section.


### Are video interviews better than phone screens?


Video interviews beat phone screens when you need to replay answers, share them, and score candidates the same way. Phone screens are quicker for simple checks, and AI-led interviews run by phone or video.


### What rating scale should you use to score video interviews?


Use a 1 to 5 scale with a written description for each score, such as 1 for no relevant example and 5 for a specific, complete answer. Score each question separately for every candidate.
